duetPrivacySections.title: How does Duet use AI?
body: AI is optional. After you accept the Terms and finish setup, Duet asks for your permission before any AI processing. You don't need to connect a health source first.

If you choose Allow AI, Coda uses third-party AI services for your Duet conversation, remembering what you share, check-ins and reminders you ask for, reviews of new information, insights, and summaries you prepare for your doctor. If you choose Not now, the rest of Duet still works. You can change your choice in Settings.

To do this, Duet uses what you write, its earlier replies, what it remembers about you, selected health facts, and relevant details from your connected records and the items you save in Duet. For a doctor summary, it uses only the information and notes you select.
Duet never sends these to AI services:

list: Raw health samples, ECG waveforms, or audiogram measurements.
Workout routes.
Original files from your sources.
Anything another person shares with you.

body: Anything you type or paste into the conversation is sent as you wrote it.

Duet keeps one private set of notes about what matters to you, such as your goals, preferences, circumstances, and ongoing concerns. The notes can also reflect your connected records. To correct them, tell Duet in the conversation. In a long conversation, Duet may also keep a shorter summary of what you discussed earlier.

You can pause AI in Settings and resume it later, or withdraw your permission to stop future AI processing. Neither deletes your records, conversation, what Duet remembers, insights, or doctor materials. Withdrawing can't recall information already sent.

OpenAI is our AI provider. Duet sends it information only after you choose Allow AI. Our agreement with OpenAI covers the handling of eligible health information. We turn off ordinary response storage and don't permit model training with your health information.

OpenAI may still keep limited information for abuse monitoring, legal obligations, and technical processing, including encrypted prompt caching for up to 24 hours. Our settings restrict human review. They don't guarantee zero retention or processing only in the United States.

duetPrivacySections.title: What happens when I connect or disconnect a source?
body: You choose Apple Health permissions by data type on your iPhone. Each MyChart organization has its own authorization and disconnect control. Connecting one doesn't give Duet access to another.
Duet keeps the source and date with your records. Information from a source may be delayed, incomplete, changed, or unavailable.
While you use Duet, it refreshes MyChart about once a day. To do this, it records when you last opened Duet. If you haven't opened Duet for seven days, automatic refreshes stop until you come back.

Disconnecting a source stops future access and updates and removes its saved credentials. It doesn't change the original source. Duet keeps the history it already imported, along with insights, doctor materials, and what it remembers, and can still use them. They stay until you delete your account. You can remove doctor materials in For my doctor.
Disconnecting MyChart in Duet doesn't confirm that Epic has revoked its authorization. To revoke access at the source, use the connected-apps controls in MyChart.

duetPrivacySections.title: How does sharing with another person work?
body: You choose what to share and with whom. Receiving someone's information doesn't give them access to yours. Duet has no public profiles, no contact discovery, and no automatic access to new health information.

Your iPhone encrypts a separate copy of the daily measurements you select for each person. The private sharing key stays on that iPhone. In normal operation, Coda stores and delivers this encrypted information without being able to read the shared values. We can see the accounts involved, which measurement types you share, and delivery timing.
Other health information in your Duet account doesn't have this end-to-end encryption.
Information shared with you stays separate from your own. It isn't used for your analytics, AI processing, doctor materials, personal comparisons, Apple Health, widgets, or account export.

duetPrivacySections.title: What do notifications show?
body: Apple delivers Duet's notifications, and they are generic. When a check-in or reminder you asked for has a reply, the alert says only "You have a new message." Notifications never include a person's name, measurement names or counts, health values, or where the information came from.

Each iPhone signed in to your account registers for notifications on its own. Check-in and reminder alerts can go to every signed-in iPhone that has notifications on. Sharing alerts go only to the iPhone that holds your private sharing key.

Signing out on an iPhone stops notifications to that iPhone. Sign out everywhere signs your account out on all devices and stops notifications to all of them. Another device may keep working for up to an hour.

duetPrivacySections.title: Do you use my information to improve Duet?
body: You can rate Duet's replies: a thumbs up, or a thumbs down with any of the listed reasons and an optional note. Your feedback stays in your account and is included in your export. Duet doesn't use it in its replies or in what it remembers.

To improve Duet, Coda uses only daily counts of how many people gave each rating and reason. We don't use your note or your conversation for these counts. Counts from fewer than five people are left out.

A day's counts don't change once recorded, and they are kept after you delete your account. They don't identify you. We keep these counts only in deidentified form and do not attempt to reidentify them.
We don't currently use connected health information for optional product-improvement or research programs. Connecting a source, using Duet, or allowing AI doesn't give that permission.

Any future program would ask for a separate, optional choice and use only the information it needs. It would exclude raw health samples, records, documents, doctor PDFs, free text, and anything another person shares with you. You could withdraw without losing core Duet features, and deleting your account would remove the related information Duet holds.

duetPrivacySections.title: How long do you keep my information?

Until you delete your account.
Doctor materials
Until you remove them in For my doctor or delete your account. Duet keeps no archive of shared PDFs.
Shared information
Until you stop sharing or delete your account.
Database backups

We back up Duet's database every day and keep the seven most recent daily backups, with seven days of recovery logs. Backups are kept for a limited time and used only for recovery. This doesn't mean every copy is gone exactly seven days after you delete your account.
Recovery records

Minimal records of a deletion or withdrawal: the account or item, the restriction, and its time. They contain no health information and are kept while an older backup could otherwise undo your choice.
Service logs

30 days for routine cloud logs, 365 days for selected security and operational records, and 400 days for required cloud audit records. Access is restricted, and health information in diagnostic logs is kept to a minimum.
Daily feedback counts
Kept after you delete your account, in deidentified form.

body: Logs aren't used as a separate health profile or research dataset.

duetTermsSections.title: Is Duet medical care?
body: No. Duet organizes your health information and can explain it, including your records, measurements, and test results. It may describe a change or pattern, or repeat a finding from a connected record. It can share general information about common causes of a symptom and published warning signs, with their uncertainty. It may also share published guidance, such as general screening recommendations, with its source.

Duet does not diagnose or monitor emergencies, and it does not judge how serious or urgent something is. It does not recommend treatment, tests, or dose changes for you. Information may be incomplete or delayed. For medical advice, contact a qualified clinician. In an emergency, call 911.
Duet also does not determine what is causing your symptoms, assess your personal medical risk or prognosis, or tell you that waiting is safe. It does not replace a qualified healthcare professional.

Duet's replies, observations, and doctor summaries are for understanding, organizing, and communicating information. They are not medical conclusions or recommendations, even when they mention warning signs or suggest talking with a doctor.

sections.title: Purpose and users
body: Chords is a physician-directed system for continuous, personalized care. It is designed to help licensed healthcare professionals maintain longitudinal patient context, recognize moments that may merit review, and carry bounded clinical work between encounters.

The current intended use of Chords is decision support for non-emergency, non-time-critical care. It is not an autonomous clinician and does not replace examination, professional judgment, or the physician-patient relationship.

sections.title: The care loop
body: With authorized connections, Chords can observe relevant records, results, messages, schedules, and selected home data. A source change, approaching encounter, due follow-up, or physician direction can give Chords a reason to review a patient's care.

Chords is designed to reconstruct the prior decision, current state, and material uncertainty; fill bounded information gaps through approved sources; and, when useful, give the physician concise evidence-linked judgment and options. It can carry an explicit follow-up forward for later reassessment while keeping completed work available for inspection.

sections.title: Information and provenance
body: Chords works only with patient information made available through authorized sources or provided by the physician. It is designed to preserve which patient facts were used, where and when they came from, and whether relevant information is current, incomplete, unavailable, or conflicting.

Patient-specific claims should remain traceable to the exact source material behind them. General medical knowledge may inform clinical reasoning, but it is not a substitute for patient evidence, and material evidence or knowledge limits should be visible to the reviewing professional.

sections.title: What the physician can review
body: Before making a decision, the physician should be able to inspect the assessment or recommendation from Chords, the patient-specific facts and sources that support it, the rationale presented, material uncertainty, reasonable alternatives and tradeoffs, relevant limitations, and any question that remains unresolved.

The physician may accept, change, reject, or ask Chords to reconsider an output. New information and physician corrections remain part of the continuing patient context rather than being treated as approval of the interpretation Chords gave earlier.

sections.title: Clinical authority
body: Chords may recommend what it would do and explain why, but it does not determine care. The licensed healthcare professional makes final decisions about diagnosis, treatment, medications, orders, and communication and approves any action that follows.

The current version of Chords does not independently send a patient message, place an order, change a medication, write back to a clinical record, or perform another clinical action. Any later action capability requires explicit, action-specific authority, workflow controls, and a governing agreement.

sections.title: Limits and validation
body: Chords is not intended for emergencies, autonomous monitoring, alarms, or time-critical directives. The current product does not analyze raw medical images, waveforms, continuous physiological signal streams, or raw diagnostic signals; any future function that does would require its own product, clinical, and regulatory review.

Clinical performance is specific to the function, intended users, patient population, information available, workflow, and setting. Before a clinical deployment, Coda Health and the participating healthcare organization must define and validate those conditions, along with known limitations, escalation paths, monitoring, security, and operational controls. Deployment-specific labeling and agreements control if they differ from this general description.

sections.title: Duet is separate
body: Duet is Coda Health's separate, patient-directed iPhone app. It helps people organize health information they choose to connect, review supported observations, and prepare information to share in a conversation with a healthcare professional.

Duet does not provide a diagnosis, personalized risk or prognosis, medical significance, urgency, treatment, testing direction, medication effect, or unsupported reassurance. Its own Terms of Service and Privacy Policy govern its use and are available at codahealth.ai/duet/terms and codahealth.ai/duet/privacy.
